fr001_live_proof.what_happened: the agent tried to write the Context Record with a shell heredoc that also piped the file through `python3 -c` to validate it. python3 is not a provably read-only program, so the whole command classified as a mutation and the gate refused it (class 8) at tool call 6, one call before the Context Record was written with the Write tool at call 7.
fr001_live_proof.old_semantics: FAIL - the attempted mutation at 6 preceded the record at 7
fr001_live_proof.new_semantics: PASS - the refused call never reached the workspace; the first effective mutation is 8
fr001_live_proof.corroboration: the host-written gate log records deny class 8 on Bash, so the response-borne refusal was corroborated and spent
fr001_live_proof.significance: this is the live production confirmation that the replay proof matches production. The focused K1 runs never exercised it, because in those the model wrote the record before touching anything (gate log all-allow).

failures.detail: the agent classified a plan-free task as `planned` (expected `direct`), so the oracle failed. classification_mismatches=1, no invariant violations, outcome still succeeded, cleanup ok.

observation_not_a_blocker.what: the gate's pre-record refusal over-reaches on a bundled command
observation_not_a_blocker.detail: K5's refused call was the agent writing the Context Record itself, bundled with a `python3 -c` JSON validation. Because python3 is not in the read-only program set, the whole command counted as a mutation and was refused, and the refusal message asked for the very record the command was writing.
observation_not_a_blocker.why_not_fixed: the refusal is a cooperative, recoverable control and the agent recovered in one step with the Write tool; K5 passed. Adding python3 to the read-only set would be a safety-relevant loosening. Pre-existing behaviour, out of T081's scope, recorded here as harness-improvement input.
